overview: Artemis is the only anticheat with logic on the send side of the resource-pack flow. Its PingSpoofProtocol pushes a fake S48 offer whose URL encodes a keepalive id and validates the client's C19 FAILED_DOWNLOAD reply, and ResourcePackTickHandler uses a level:// offer with a numeric hash as a tick-confirmation channel. These are the OUT-side arms of the same two checks documented on the C19PacketResourcePackStatus page. FlopAC's WrappedOutResourcePackSend and the Negativity RESOURCE_PACK_SEND constant are wrappers and registrations only.

checks.name: PingSpoofProtocol (Artemis)
checks.purpose: Detect ping spoofing with a resource-pack offer as the probe: the server sends S48 with an id-encoded URL and verifies the client's C19 answer.
checks.how_it_works: On 1.9 and older servers the check builds a GPacketPlayServerResourcePackSend whose URL is a generated numeric id (line 175) and pushes it to the client. It then expects the C19 response: FAILED_DOWNLOAD with a matching numeric URL, followed by the next keepalive echo. Missing, out-of-order or non-numeric responses log violations. On 1.10+ it switches to fake teleports because the packet's hash field was removed there.
checks.detects: Ping spoofers that suppress or reorder keepalives, and clients that answer resource-pack offers they were never sent.
checks.variations: ResourcePackTickHandler is the non-flagging sibling that reuses the probe as a tick counter; FlopAC and Negativity only register the packet.

checks.name: ResourcePackTickHandler (Artemis)
checks.purpose: Use a level:// resource-pack offer as a tick-confirmation channel on 1.8 servers.
checks.how_it_works: On 1.8.9 and below it sends a GPacketPlayServerResourcePackSend whose hash encodes a numeric tick id (line 57), then accepts only C19 FAILED_DOWNLOAD replies whose URL is numeric and contains the player name. The parsed id is stored as the player's resourcePackTick and feeds the tick-confirmation infrastructure other Artemis checks use to measure connection state.
checks.detects: Nothing directly. It feeds connection-state measurement rather than flagging a behavior.
checks.variations: PingSpoofProtocol is the flagging version of the same mechanism; FlopAC WrappedOutResourcePackSend is a plain wrapper over the packet fields.
